prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1050; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the policyholder's driver reporting a low-speed collision in a parking lot with another vehicle, with a head injury described as a concussion. Claimant is not represented by counsel at this time.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of the reported loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant, who described the same sequence of events as in the initial report, including the approximate speed and the point of impact. The account has not changed across contacts.

Entry 4: Police report on file lists the claimant as an occupant of the vehicle at the scene, and a responding officer's notes match the described position of both cars.

Entry 5: Reviewed photographs submitted by the claimant. They confirm several details of the impact, including the location of the damage and the resting positions of the vehicles.

Entry 6: No independent witnesses have come forward. Asked the claimant for any other sources of information and will follow up if anything is produced.

Entry 7: Damage to the vehicle is mostly consistent with the impact described. Obtained a repair estimate from the body shop and am comparing it against the photos.

Entry 8: Checked prior loss history on the vehicle. No earlier damage to this vehicle is known to exist.

Entry 9: Claimant reports a concussion from the collision, with headaches and dizziness in the days that followed. The reported injury is plausible for a collision of this type.

Entry 10: Medical records show a course of treatment that followed a usual pattern, with visits tapering as symptoms improved. Records also note a minor strain to the same general area several years ago, which resolved fully with no ongoing issues.

Entry 11: Discussed the prior strain with the claimant, who confirmed it and said it had healed completely. The treating provider's notes support that account, and the current injury appears separate from it.

Entry 12: Claim review is on hold pending the final medical bills and the repair invoice. Current assessment is that the reported loss and injury are consistent with the available evidence.
